summary.headline: Quality update policy remains for advanced servicing scenarios
summary.summary: Quality update policies are positioned for advanced deployments such as Hotpatch or Windows Autopatch-managed workflows rather than ordinary monthly servicing.
summary.adminImpact: Create a quality update policy when Hotpatch or Autopatch-managed servicing is required; otherwise use standard Windows Update controls.

summary.headline: Defender for Endpoint integration is framed around device compliance
summary.summary: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration guidance now emphasizes Mobile Threat Defense device compliance and preventing security breaches.
summary.adminImpact: Use the integration to feed Defender device risk into Intune compliance decisions.

summary.headline: Defender integration requires an Intune role with sufficient permissions
summary.summary: The prerequisites clarify that the administrator needs an Intune role able to configure the settings and cite Endpoint Security Manager as an example.
summary.adminImpact: Assign an appropriately privileged Intune role before configuring Defender for Endpoint integration.

summary.headline: Defender onboarding guidance is framed as configuration
summary.summary: The onboarding guidance is titled Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and Onboard Devices.

summary.headline: Defender risk workflow references Microsoft Defender XDR
summary.summary: The integration guidance identifies the Microsoft Defender XDR portal for subscription access and threat reports, while retaining the high-risk device flow that lets Intune remove corporate-resource access.
summary.adminImpact: Ensure operations teams use the Defender XDR portal when investigating a Defender high-risk signal that affects Intune access.
